title: Paged KV liveness probing and warmup policy for steady-state continuous batching
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: In oversubscribed GPU hosts we see periodic latency spikes caused by unexpectedly cold KV pages being touched during continuous batching bursts. Existing eviction and prefetch heuristics are reactive and operate at coarse granularity, causing head-of-line token stalls and degraded p95 latency for short bursts.

Goal: Implement a lightweight liveness probing and graded warmup policy for paged/blocked KV so the serving runtime can proactively bring the right page granularity into GPU residency before a batch that will touch them is scheduled. This should integrate with continuous batching and the batch scheduler to attach prefetch hints, operate within thermal and residency budgets, and expose observability to evaluate warmup accuracy and cost trade-offs.

High-level approach:
1) Liveness probes: add a two-tier probe that first checks a small metadata residency bitmap (cheap host-side) and, if ambiguous, issues a low-priority device-residency probe for a representative token in the page. Probes are rate-limited per-token-affinity lane and piggybacked on existing host-to-device scatter queues to avoid extra host-device round trips.
2) Graded warmup levels: define three warmup actions for a targeted page/block: METADATA (ensure headers and pointers are resident), PARTIAL (hot kv-slices for the first N tokens of the page), FULL (bring entire block). The batch scheduler selects level by predicted token footprint and SLA tier.
3) Predictive warmup window: derive expected touched pages from the request prefix and recent token-affinity heatmaps. Use a rolling 30s EWMA of page-touch frequency and a per-route short-term predictor to decide warmup candidates.
4) Host-accelerated prefetch threads: use bounded host threads to perform async host staging and DMA-prefetch to GPU pages across PCIe/NVLink. In low-memory hosts, fall back to host-resident KDOL (keep-on-host) path with incremental streaming to device as tokens are consumed.
5) Scheduler integration: extend continuous batcher to carry warmup hints and an optional timeout that, if expired, downgrades warmup to METADATA or cancels it. Warmup work is considered in slot allocation to avoid sudden eviction pressure.

Trade-offs considered: extra host memory consumption for staging, increased PCIe traffic, potential misprediction cost versus reduced cold-miss p95 impact, complexity of coordinating warmup with eviction and checkpointing. We prefer conservative defaults (METADATA by default) and enable escalating warmup only for routes flagged high-SLA or high-affinity by the predictor.

Observability: instrument new metrics: kv_probe_latency_ms, warmup_action_count{metadata,partial,full}, warmup_accuracy_ratio (pages warmed that were actually used), cold_miss_penalty_ms, page_stall_rate, gpu_swap_count, batch_p95_with_warmup, extra_pci_bytes_warmup. Add dashboards and an alert when warmup_accuracy_ratio < 0.2 and extra_pci_bytes_warmup exceeds a budget.

Rollout plan: canary on dedicated capacity pool A with synthetic burst tests (see test plan), then opt-in for selected tenants, enabling warmup for non-critical routes to gather signals, finally enable for high-SLA routes after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Probes can classify page residency with >95% accuracy for metadata-only checks within 50us median host time
Warmup actions reduce cold-miss-induced token stall tail latency (batch_p95) by >=35% in burst simulations without increasing average batch latency by >5%
Metrics and dashboard exist for all warmup metrics and a synthetic canary test that validates warmup_accuracy_ratio and extra_pci_bytes_warmup
Graceful fallback to host-resident streaming when device residency budget would be violated
Unit and integration tests for probe paths, warmup escalation/downgrade, and scheduler cancellation hooks merged and passing
comments: 2026-03-05 Sofia Martinez: Initial ticket created after postmortem from 2026-03-03 burst incident. Noted that multiple routes had correlated cold page touches from shared prefixes.
2026-03-06 Rahul Iyer: Prototype of metadata bitmap probe implemented. Observed ~12-18us median on host for 8k page-map checks. Added rate limiter to avoid probe storms.
2026-03-08 Design review (with Camille): agreed to three warmup levels and to keep METADATA as default to limit PCIe overhead. Camille asked for clear UX in Console to show 'warmup cost' per route.
2026-03-09 Perf note: microbench synthetic shows partial warmup reduces first-token stall by 42% for sequences with locality; full warmup is only beneficial when >75% of page tokens are used.
2026-03-11 Security: KMS/HSM not impacted but noted that logs may show additional page touch metadata; scrub sensitive prompt content from warmup telemetry per privacy policy.
2026-03-12 Rahul Iyer: Integration tests added for scheduler hint attachment and cancellation. Preparing canary PR: github.com/redwood/serve/pull/2783
decisions: Default warmup action is METADATA to minimize PCIe overhead for unknown routes
Warmup escalation requires both predictor score > 0.7 and free_device_residency_budget > threshold
Host-staged DMA prefetch is preferred on NVLink-capable hosts; PCIe-only hosts fallback to incremental streaming
